traditions.label: Hebrew (biblical names)
traditions.description: Two traditional identifications from Job and Amos, shown as catalogue locator rings; disputed terms remain unlocated.
traditions.historicalScope: Biblical Hebrew attestations, with later interpretive identifications kept explicit.
traditions.geometryNotice: Rings identify selected modern catalogue members of the conventionally identified groups. The cited biblical passages preserve neither these memberships nor connecting lines. No ancient Hebrew outline is claimed.

source.authors: Mazzaroth project compilation from the cited primary texts
source.authorsText: Hebrew names are attested in the Hebrew Bible or medieval Hebrew astronomical texts. Source identifications, chosen catalogue locators, and modern reference geometry are distinguished in each record. All notes are new paraphrases; no modern translation passages are redistributed.
source.licenseText: This new selection, arrangement and annotation is provided under CC BY-SA 4.0. The ancient names and historical facts remain subject to their own public-domain status. Modern reference geometry, where used, is from the Stellarium team under CC BY-SA 4.0 and is separately credited; no rights in cited websites or modern translations are asserted.
source.changes: New evidence-based comparison compilation. Cited texts supply names, not a recovered Hebrew line atlas. Modern catalogue locators and borrowed reference geometry are explicitly identified.

constellations.name: Kīmāh · Pleiades
constellations.status: Traditional identification; locator membership is modern
constellations.notes: Kimah is named in Job 9:9, Job 38:31, and Amos 5:8. JPS 1917 renders the name as Pleiades. Nine familiar catalogue members locate that conventional identification; the ancient passages do not specify this list. The stars are shown separately, with no invented connecting outline.

unlocated.name: ʿAsh / ʿAyish
unlocated.notes: Job 9:9 names Ash; Job 38:32 names Ayish with its children. JPS 1917 renders these as the Bear, but Berakhot 58b:15 records competing identifications of Ash/Yota in the tail of Aries or head of Taurus. A fixed Ursa Major, Hyades, or other outline is therefore not assigned in this layer.

traditions.label: Hebrew (medieval zodiac)
traditions.description: Twelve attested Hebrew zodiac names on modern reference outlines, kept separate from the biblical-name layer.
traditions.historicalScope: Medieval Hebrew astronomical naming, documented in Maimonides (12th century); corroborated by a Sefer Yetzirah recension.
traditions.geometryNotice: Modern Western line figures provide comparison geometry only. They are not transmitted Hebrew outlines and are not the equal 30-degree zodiac divisions used in medieval calculations. Changing the sky epoch does not redetermine the historical date of the source.
